## Video 1 — Your introduction (60–90 seconds)
**Title:** Before you solve it, understand it.

**Script:**

“I have tried many things in my life. Some worked, and others did not. One thing I kept noticing was that I often wanted a solution before I had fully understood the problem.

Think of a person who keeps changing businesses because nothing seems to work. Maybe the problem is not a lack of ideas. Maybe they have not understood their customers, their costs, or what they can sustain.

That experience shaped a framework I am developing. I call it ASSSS: Awareness, Strategy, Structure, Systems, and Success.

I don't believe every problem has an easy answer. But I believe better questions can help us avoid costly mistakes.

I'm hm hamzury. On this page, I'll share what I am learning about business, technology, institutions, and life.

What is one problem you think people rush to solve without understanding?”

**Caption:** Before we solve a problem, we should understand what is really happening. I am developing ASSSS through learning, building and questioning. What problem should we examine together? #ASSSS #hmhamzury #ProblemSolving

**Recording:** Chest-up frame; natural daylight; speak deliberately; no dramatic background music. TikTok and Instagram Reel first; adapt the transcript to LinkedIn/Facebook only if it is useful.

## Video 2 — A lesson in entrepreneurship (45–75 seconds)
**Title:** A logo is not a business strategy.

**Script:**

“Let me ask you a question. If someone wants to start a business, what should come first: a logo, or understanding the customer?

I have seen how easy it is to focus on the visible parts: the name, logo, flyers and social media. Those things can be important, but they don't tell us whether anybody needs what we want to sell.

In ASSSS, I would start with Awareness. Who has this problem? How serious is it? What are they doing now? And what evidence do we have?

Then Strategy: what are we choosing to offer, to whom, and why?

Before you spend money designing everything, talk to five potential customers and write down what you learn.

What would you ask them?”

**Caption:** Branding matters. Understanding the customer comes first. One exercise: speak with five potential customers before making big commitments. #Entrepreneurship #ASSSS #hmhamzury

## Video 3 — Why I teach (60–90 seconds)
**Title:** Skills need somewhere to go.

**Script:**

“One reason I care about entrepreneurship and technology education is that learning should create more possibilities for people.

A student may learn how to build a website or use AI tools, but still struggle to identify a real problem, organise a project, communicate with clients or show evidence of what they can do.

That is why, when I teach students at Hamzury Hub, I want us to connect knowledge to practice. Awareness: understand the problem. Strategy: decide what matters. Structure: organise the work. Systems: make the process dependable. Success: check what actually changed.

A certificate may mark learning. But I also want to see capability.

If you are learning a new skill, what practical thing can you build with it this week?”

**Caption:** Learning becomes more meaningful when we can demonstrate what we know. At the Hub, I want entrepreneurship and technology students to connect learning with real problems. #DigitalSkills #EntrepreneurshipEducation #ASSSS

## Five-slide carousel — the first stage
1. **Before you solve it, understand it.**
2. The problem you see may be a symptom.
3. Ask: What do I know? What am I assuming?
4. Speak to the people affected; examine evidence.
5. Awareness is not having the answer. It is asking better questions. — hm hamzury
